sections.h2: Who handles your Mecklenburg property tax
sections.html:
Value and billing live in different buildings. Tax Administration sets the number and takes appeals, while the Tax Collector sends the bill and collects the money. Everything lands on one combined bill from the Collector, covering county tax plus the levies of Charlotte, Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville, Matthews, Mint Hill and Pineville.

With an escrow account, your servicer receives the bill and you only get a notice. Ask the servicer which tax year it has already paid before you sell, so the closing attorney works from real numbers.

Mecklenburg is a large, fast-growing market: 1,233,383 people in mid 2025, with 538,576 housing units. Just over half of homes (55.1 percent) are lived in by their owners, and the median owner-occupied value was $406,800 across 2020 to 2024. Because one reappraisal touches so many parcels, the county posts a lot of guidance online, and the steps below pull the seller-relevant parts together.

The yearly pattern is steady. Bills are mailed in late July and are due September 1. Interest stays off until after January 5 (G.S. 105-360 is the rule behind that cutoff). On January 6 the bill picks up 2 percent. Each month after that adds 0.75 percent until the balance is cleared.

Yearly rhythm of a Mecklenburg County bill
DateEvent
January 1Value and ownership fixed for the year
Late JulyBills mailed
September 1Payment due
January 5Final day without interest
January 6Interest of 2 percent begins
February onAnother 0.75 percent each month

If you expect to come up short, contact Tax Administration well before December rather than waiting for interest to start.

Four routes exist. A card payment carries a vendor fee, and an e-check carries none.

  • Online at MeckNC.gov/PayTax.
  • By phone at 1-800-994-1026.
  • By post, using the envelope enclosed with the bill.
  • In person at the Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3000, between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays. Make checks payable to the Mecklenburg County Tax Collector.

Skip your bank's bill pay if you can. A payment that bounces back cannot have its interest waived, and a bank transfer can take four business days to arrive. Billing questions go to 704-336-7600.

Mecklenburg revalues every four years, twice as often as G.S. 105-286 requires. Commissioners set January 1, 2027 as the value date.

By the fall 2026 update, 428,506 parcels had been through a first review. Median movement was about 15 percent up for houses and about 30 percent up for commercial property. Notices of Value are planned for early 2027, and the county and municipal boards set rates in spring. A higher value need not mean an equal jump in your bill, since the rate can fall.

Your property record card is online at Reval.MeckNC.gov, so look there first. The county's own example is a home credited with three bathrooms that really has two. Fixing a record before notices mail is far easier than arguing with a number afterward.

Appraisers watch market data and compare property sales when they set new values, so recent sales near your house matter once notices arrive.

Send appeals to the Office of Tax Administration, which passes them to the county's equalization board (BER). During a reappraisal, nothing can be filed until Notices of Value are mailed, and your notice prints its own deadline. Other years, the cutoff is the Board's adjournment. Here is the county's sequence:

  • Sign the Formal Appeal Form and submit it by email, by mail to BER Real Property Appeals, P.O. Box 31127, Charlotte, NC 28231, or in person at the Woodard Center, Suite 3500.
  • Add evidence at filing or within 45 days.
  • Watch the mail for a hearing letter roughly 30 days ahead.
  • Ask for any continuance within 10 days of that letter.
  • A written ruling should arrive inside 30 days. If you still disagree, take the case to the state's Property Tax Commission within another 30 days.

You must prove the assessment is too high. State timing rules for real property appeals sit in G.S. 105-322 and G.S. 105-290.

Vehicles and business property follow other tracks. For a registered vehicle you have 30 days after the due date shown on the combined tax and registration notice. Start with an informal email request, and pay the full tax before any hearing. Business and individual personal property can be disputed in the 30 days after the first notice of value.

Three state programs exist, and one is all you may hold. Apply for any of them with Form AV-9 at the county assessor.

  • Age or disability exclusion: cuts the taxable amount by $25,000 or by half the value if that is greater. You must be 65 or over, or permanently disabled, with 2026 income no higher than $38,800 (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: takes $45,000 from the taxable value and asks nothing about age or income (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: once you have lived there five years, the bill is limited to 4 or 5 percent of income and the excess waits, deferred, until a transfer (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Ask the assessor whether your parcel carries a deferral. It becomes payable at transfer, so your attorney needs that amount along with the mortgage payoff.

Each year's tax becomes a lien on January 1, and penalties and interest follow it (G.S. 105-355). It stays on the parcel and passes to a buyer. If ignored, it can end in a court foreclosure.

Even a fall closing can leave the seller owing that year's bill. Let the settlement statement spell out who pays which months, and request a payoff from the Collector ahead of closing. Recording and excise tax are the Register of Deeds' business and have their own page.

If you are carrying back taxes, an open appeal or a bill you cannot cover, a written cash offer lets you pick a closing date around the tax calendar. Before any call, round up three papers: your latest bill, any AV-9 on file and the deed. Then ask the Collector for the current-year payoff and for any earlier years, and ask Tax Administration whether an appeal is still open on the parcel.

faqs.q: Which date matters more for Mecklenburg County taxes, September 1 or January 5?
faqs.a: Both. September 1 is the due date, and January 5 is the last day with no interest. After that, 2 percent applies from January 6, followed by 0.75 percent each month.

faqs.q: When can I file an appeal after the 2027 notices go out?
faqs.a: Right away. In a reappraisal year filing opens once Notices of Value are mailed, and the notice states your last date. Attach evidence to the Formal Appeal Form or send it within 45 days.

faqs.q: Is there a walk-in counter for paying a Mecklenburg bill?
faqs.a: Yes, at the Valerie C. Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3000, Charlotte, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Cash, cards, money orders and checks are taken.

faqs.q: Will a new value mean my bill rises by the same percentage?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Tax equals value times rate, and rates are set in spring after values post. Compare the new rates with your new value before reacting.

faqs.q: Do seniors in Mecklenburg County get any property tax reduction?
faqs.a: They can. An owner 65 or older with income at or below $38,800 for 2026 may claim the state exclusion of $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is larger. Apply on Form AV-9 with the assessor, and note that only one state program may be used.
